_about: Demo D (How a lost tag is found). Single source for the static table in m05.html (written by scripts/invisible_engine/content/inserts.py) and for lost.js; tested by invisible-engine/tests/demos.mjs. Values follow Apple's documented Find My network design (Apple Platform Security guide); 'meta' means metadata only, never the location.

steps.title: The tag is alone
steps.text: A suitcase sits at a station. Its tag has no GPS and no mobile connection, so it does not know where it is. It only whispers a changing identifier over Bluetooth.

steps.title: A stranger walks past
steps.text: A passer-by’s phone overhears the whisper. It does not pair with the tag. It uses its own location services to estimate where it (the phone) is, and seals that location so only the tag’s owner can open it.

steps.title: The sealed report is stored
steps.text: The phone uploads the sealed report, filed under a lookup value made from the identifier. The relay stores it but cannot open it.

steps.title: The owner opens it
steps.text: Later, the owner’s signed-in device works out which identifiers its tag would have used, fetches the matching sealed reports and opens them locally: an estimated location and a time, not a live feed.

items.label: The changing identifier the tag broadcasts
items.note: Broadcast in the clear by design; it changes over time so it is hard to follow. The relay receives only a lookup value derived from it. The owner’s device can regenerate it.

items.label: Lookup value (a hash of the identifier)
items.note: How a sealed report is filed and found. Anyone who heard the identifier could compute it, but it opens nothing.

items.label: The location in the report (where the finder was)
items.note: The finder knows its own location; only the owner’s device can decrypt the report. Apple says it cannot read the locations.

items.label: The sealed (encrypted) report
items.note: Created by the finder, stored by the relay, opened by the owner’s device.

items.label: When the report was made or uploaded
items.note: Upload timing is service metadata even when the content is sealed.

items.label: Who the finder is
items.note: Apple says reports do not identify the finder. Network connections still carry ordinary connection metadata.

items.label: Whose tag it is (the owner’s account)
items.note: The finder never learns the owner. The account that signs in to fetch reports is known to the service.
